According to Kenya’s National Food and Nutrition Security Policy (2012), more 10 million Kenyans suffer from chronic food insecurity and poor nutrition. Between 2 and 4 million people require emergency food assistance at any given time. Nearly 30% of Kenya’s children are undernourished and micro-nutrient deficiencies are widespread.

The Constitution of Kenya recognizes that each one of us has a right to adequate food. Despite our
constitutional commitment, national legislation, policy and practice fail to implement and monitor solutions to food security. 

We need to change the course of action from chronic hunger, industrial agriculture and food aid, to a discussion about food rights and accountability.

We cannot let our people starve to death and not raise our voices against it. Life and death. We cannot be quiet about it.  And it's time we discuss it.

We are taking a stand against the politics of food, because it is immoral that the benchmark for life rests on the threshold of survival.

Let this song spark a conversation and open up the minds and hearts of all Kenyans to speak out against this chronic food security problem that is crippling our nation.

Let's all come together and work towards realising our human right  to food for every man,woman and child.

Special mention & acknowledgement to the Route To Food Alliance for joining and helping us push this agenda.

title: #ElaniSpeaks - Where We Have Been
description:
We have been silent for a long time. After a successful year and several releases we realized that a loophole exists in the industry. A problem affecting musicians must be discussed. 

The structures within the music industry in Kenya have failed the musician. Those entrusted to distribute the money which is generated by our hard work have failed us. The organizations whose sole purpose is to manage and distribute the funds that our blood, sweat and tears have created have failed us. We spent all we had to make the best music we could. We sincerely deserve to get our due. 

Being a musician is a job. It is an investment. It takes an incredible amount of time, money, persistence and effort. It needs to make sense. But we are stuck in a vicious cycle where a song is played and the finances owed to the creator are stuck in a black hole that can't quite be found. As it stands, a select few continue to siphon money that artists have worked hard to earn. The money generated disappears and finds its way into pockets that are not ours.

We are not giving our all, only to sit back and watch another person buy a new Range Rover by our sweat. So we need to change the structure. 

#ElaniSpeaks about the #TruthAboutMCSK.
Something needs to change.

title: (TRIBUTE) ELANI PEPERUKA CHOREOGRAPHED BY SULE
description:
We came across this story and we just had to share this with you "when i was two ,i was walking out of my room on day and my mum whispered something to me.She told me to always be strong,responsible,loving,respectful and to work hard always.I never understood why but i was two,that kid who was always thinking of movies and playing alot plus coming back home with dusty feet,I would get a good whooping but as a kid,this was the story of my life.Mum was always there when i needed her.
One day when i was from school,i found her crying and a did not get why? I kept asking as usual when she was sad and i  would take a comb and do her hair as usual and we would talk for hours but this time it did not work.So i went to my sister and asked her what was wrong.She went silent on me and a felt like they were hiding something from me.The very next day,i saw a casket and i went like whose casket is this for and thats when she told me that it was my father. My heart sunk .Losing someone you love is so painful pain but i  had to be strong and accept it and live with it.as i  was very young.Nothing to me remained the same after that day.Life was great back then but mum had to take charge and it was not easy because we were five children plus her.She never  gave up on us.I remember a day she came and some dude snached her purse and she was crying.I remember giving her five shillings that i  had saved up and she was so proud and happy.she was my everything,my first love and no one will ever take her place. It was during ma K.C,S.E when she passed and it broke me and till now am trying to work on that but how a wish to just see her smile again,just one more time and hold her and tell her how a love and miss her,but one day a know we will be re-united.Love you mum and dad though i didn't get to know you better dad,i hope i have not let you down in any way.This peace i have done is for you. I got to listen to this song by Elani and it brought back memories that a had done away with.I am thankful to ELANI for this beautiful song and my family who have been there for me and THE BAND AHOOOO .Thank you for everything love you guys. "

description:
The song "Ndiwike" is an ode to the weekend, a time of celebration and release after a week of hard work. The title itself is a clever play on words, reversing the English word "weekend" to create the Swahili term "Wikendi," which means the same thing. This linguistic twist reflects the song's fusion of Kenyan and Western influences, capturing the spirit of Nairobi's vibrant nightlife. Through its infectious beats and descriptive lyrics, "Ndiwike" transports listeners to the heart of the city's urban energy, painting a vivid picture of how young people unwind and embrace the weekend's carefree atmosphere. It's a celebration of life, a tribute to the joy of letting go and embracing the moment, and a testament to the power of music to unite people across cultures and backgrounds.

title: FEMI ONE LAUNCHES THE ONE FOR ONE FOUNDATION
description:
On Tuesday 14th of February, Rapper and AFRIMMA best femcee, Femi One, officially launched The One For One Foundation with a mentorship event at her former primary school- Murema Primary in Mwiki, Kasarani.

Femi One was also joined by fellow musician Trio Mio who got to engage with the young boys on the role they have within their growing community. 

Speaking about One For One Foundation,

Femi One 

About One For One Foundation 
Our mission is to empower the youth to overcome poverty through the cultivation and realization of their talents and dreams. We believe that every young person has the potential to succeed and we are committed to providing them with the resources, support, and opportunities they need to unleash their full potential. Whether it's through education, skill-building programs, mentorship, or other means, we will work tirelessly to help young people break free from the constraints of poverty and achieve their aspirations. Together, we will build a brighter future for all.

PARTY TIME: THE MOVIE created by H_ART THE BAND, developed & animated by the ever so talented BACKBENCH ANIMATIONS, OBY AFRIKA  and final edit/gfx by CALI DIGITAL for H_ART THE BAND'S fourth studio album: PARTY TIME. A celebration of life, love & wins whether big or small as described by the trio in an interview by the pulse magazine. 
PARTY TIME: THE MOVIE is an animated 8 chapter musical masterpiece that follows the trio on a night out, up and about. From riding through the city on the backs of three gracious Black & White beauties of the jungle the playing live in their favourite joint, H_art the Bar, alongside Dj Madlion to alighting a bachelorette party in a pimped-up matatu to jumping off their jet & deploying parachutes into a Yacht party. 
Honestly, 26mins have never gone by so fast. When asked about the inspiration, Kenchez didn't mince his words," No one can dispute the fact that Pictures speak louder than words. And, overtime different artists have used different forms of media to articulate their words & melodies. Being a lovers of animation from eversince, its always been our dream to have an animated musical album. 
PARTY TIME: THE MOVIE is a Dream Come True!"

description:
A NOTE FROM THE BAND: 
06.05.2022 marks a special day in our lives & careers. What started out as three young, broke talented friends hanging out & jamming on the steps of Kenya National Theatre has evolved to what we are now; artists cum entrepreneurs. All thanks to your love & support. 
Over time, We have grown immensely. Along the way, We have met amazing people, visited beautiful places here & abroad, boarded a plane for the first time then many times thereafter and performed on stages that seemed like a far fetched dream back in our single room in Kayole. 
A BIG THANK YOU & SHOEKRAN SANA to all of you for your Love & Support. You are the real MVP’s!!!

May this album ‘PARTY TIME’ bring you joy, happiness, & on those lonely days wipe away your tear as it has for us. 

Cheers to sleepless night. Cheers to mistakes that shaped us. Cheers to Endless walks with our guitar on our back. And Most of all, cheers to you all for being the superheroes in our journey - none of this would have been possible without you. 
Truly, Dreams do come true & we are living proof.
‘PARTY TIME’ consists of 8tracks carefully selected & curated to help spread Love, Peace, Positive vibes & surely infect you with Happiness beyond belief. 

Ladies & Rastamen

title: H_ART THE BAND - MY JABER (AMAPIANO REMIX) ft. DJ LYTA & BRIZY ANNECHILD
description:
DJ Lyta, real names Samuel Mwangi and the second-born of five siblings, never dreamt of becoming a DJ when he was young. However, his life took an unexpected turn when he started experimenting with VirtualDJ, a music mixing software, and after a six-month audio production course Lyta immersed himself in his new-found passion. Creating head-banging, half-hour music mixes and distributing them in well-labeled compact discs to matatus plying the Kayole route, where he lived with his dad. Streetblast Volume 1, which featured top reggae hits of the day, was the first music mix he created and was first played in a matatu in mid-2012.
Months later when H_art the Band also hailing from Kayole released their first song & Monster-hit ‘ULIZA KIATU’ . Dj Lyta now well known & respected in the streets was one of the People who played it on high rotation in his Matata mixes. Even without constant interaction, there still was an unspoken respect between these artists.

Years later With the rise on amapiano in Kenya, H_art the Band went on to release, MY JABER ft. @brizyannechild1lepaa off their album ‘SIMPLE MAN’ - a song to celebrate the woman, her beauty & the local lake basin Kenyan sound. This song went on to become The Biggest Kenyan Song of 2021: the video garnering 1Million views in a week, a first for the Kenyan music Industry.

Dj Lyta Loved this song so much that he requested for the files & went on to recreate this amapiano version in celebration of this feat by his counterparts from Kayole doing big in the industry.

Listen, Like, Comment & Share.

title: Victoria Kimani - HOW I DO
description:
Victoria Kimani is back with her long awaited lead single from her upcoming 5th Album. "How I Do" , Produced by Kayo Musiq, is a AfroPop/R&B Vibey Blend, signature to Kimani's eclectic, Pan African style, Her vocals flow effortlessly, declaring her unique attributes, bursting personality & self worth, embracing who you are as an individual & Taking judgement from no one, dancing to the tune of her own, boldly stating,  that's just "How I do".

Bio: 

 Victoria Kimani is a Pan-Afric International Artist originally from Kenya, East Africa,  Her music is a fusion of sounds that have appealed to her throughout her upbringing & travels. The award winning Singer-Songwriter has released 4 albums & collaborated & written for with a plethora of Afrobeat & International artists worldwide. The first ever East African Maybelline NY Ambassador was involved with the few artists selected to perform on the mega platform Coke Studio by Coca cola for two consecutive years. Victoria Kimani was also involved in Bono's One Campaign for two years standing with Women and Girls across Africa as well as promoting Agriculture, Sexism & Poverty along side U2's Bono and other Top African artists. Speaking at the UN in NYC for Female and youth Inclusion in Africa and being able to be a voice against rape culture, are some of the Star's most dear causes and a driving force in Kimani's present day goals. Victoria Kimani remains a household name in the Afro-Pop music scene, with her 5th Album to be released in 2023 and it’s prospective Lead Single “How I do” released May 2023.

Victoria Kimani, born in Los Angeles, California is originally from Kenya. She started writing, recording and performing music at the age of 16. Following her high school years in Nigeria, she moved back to Nairobi for a short while, with the intention to pursue her music full time.

Although, she travelled between Los Angeles, Atlanta, New York and London working with top line artists and producers including Chris Brown and Timberland amongst others. In 2010, she performed a cover of Ice Prince’s hit song OLEKU and from this caught the attention of Chocolate City executives. By the end of 2012, Victoria was signed on as Chocolate City Kenya’s first lady and has since been relocated to Kenya.

Bio: Guardian Angel is a Kenyan top Gospel Musician, Songwriter and multi-talented Instrumentalist, he plays both the guitar and piano.

With a music career spanning more than six years and a host of award nominations locally and in the greater East African region, Guardian Angel has released several chart topping songs that have placed him among major household names on Kenya’s music scene. Guardian Angel describes his music as music for the soul that seeks to encourage people to believe in God and bring them back to God’s presence through repentance, true worship and praise. His main fuel for this passion is to do music that is relevant now and many more years to come.

Rising from too much talk of him being the most underrated artiste in Kenya, in the year 2017 he proved the naysayers otherwise by releasing – Nadeka, a song that catapulted him onto the national scene once again, it ruled the airwaves for months leading him to ink several corporate partnerships and was listed to headline some of the biggest NYE shows in December 2017.

Wanavokali  debuts their single, Rhumba, off of their  Self-Titled Album (Wanavokali:The Album)
 
Wanavokali’s long awaited first solo single, Rhumba, is the newest entry into an emerging body of music paying homage to the golden era of Rhumba music and culture. 

A soundtrack to a fun night out in Nairobi, with its characteristic guitar licks and groovy baselines, 'Rhumba' tells the story of two strangers whose passions have been ignited, dancing the night away. Set against the back drop of smooth silky vocals and laced with modern trap beats, the feel-good party song is a constant reminder that you do not need money to have a good time and that it is always the right time to “shoot-your-shot”. 

From their new and fresh Group Vocal sound to their energetic delivery, Wanavokali successfully make their submission to the familiar and nostalgic sound from their Kenyan roots, bringing an urban and youthful twist to it that promises to make you move.
